title: Renewable and Non-renewable Energy

standard_text: Energy resources for generating electricity (coal, oil, natural gas, nuclear, hydro, geothermal, solar, wind, biomass); their advantages and disadvantages; environmental impacts; energy efficiency and conservation. key_big: Fossil fuels release carbon dioxide when burned.

body_html:
How to think about it

Most of the world's electricity comes from fossil fuels (coal, oil and natural gas), which are non-renewable and release carbon dioxide and pollutants. Nuclear power uses uranium and makes radioactive waste.

Renewable resources (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biomass) produce little carbon dioxide but may depend on the weather or location. Choosing an energy mix means weighing cost, reliability and environmental impact; using energy efficiently saves resources.

Example

A lamp uses 100 J and gives 20 J of light. Efficiency?

20/100 × 100%

Answer: 20%

Example

Which resource depends on the weather?

Clouds

Answer: solar power

Common mistakes

  • Thinking renewable energy has no impact at all.
  • Thinking nuclear power releases a lot of carbon dioxide.
  • Forgetting that efficiency is never 100%.
